chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, raising it, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafour, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the woman, and I do not know her state, can the man marry her with Mut'ah? He said: He presents himself to her, so if she responds to him with immorality (fajur), then he should not do it.

key_terms.أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Mut'ah marriage with a woman of unknown chastity?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that for Mut'ah with a woman of uncertain status, the key criterion is her response to the proposal; if she exhibits 'fajur' (promiscuity or lack of chastity), the contract is invalid. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the woman's active consent and moral character as prerequisites for the validity of temporary marriage, distinguishing it from permanent marriage where broader conditions apply. The term 'fajur' here is interpreted by jurists as a sign of unworthiness for the specific sanctity of the Mut'ah bond.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, raising it, from Abdullah Bin Abu Yafour, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws, said, ‘I asked himasws about the woman, and I do not know of her state, can the man marry her with Mut’a?’
He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘He can present (immorality) to her, so if she were to respond (positively) to the immoralities, so he should not do it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from in a marfu’ manner from ‘Abd Allah ibn abu Ya’fur who has said the following: “This is concerning my question before abu ‘Abd Allah, Alayhi al-Salam, about the case of a woman whose condition is not known; if a man can marry her in the manner of al-Mut‘ah (advantageous marriage).
He (the Imam) said, ‘He can propose unlawful activities; if she agreed, he then must stay away from her.’”
